name: Cancelable Biometrics Benchmark for Deep Templates
description: In this paper, we benchmark several cancelable biometrics (CB) schemes on different biometric characteristics. We consider BioHashing, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) Hashing, Bloom Filters, and two schemes based on Index-of-Maximum (IoM) Hashing (i.e., IoM-URP and IoM-GRP). In addition to the mentioned CB schemes, we introduce a CB scheme (as a baseline) based on user-specific random transformations followed by binarization. We evaluate the unlinkability, irreversibility, and recognition performance (which are the required criteria by the ISO/IEC 24745 standard) of these CB schemes on deep learning based templates extracted from different physiological and behavioral biometric characteristics including face, voice, finger vein, and iris. In addition, we provide an open-source implementation of all the experiments presented to facilitate the reproducibility of our results.
evaluation_method: biometric/security metrics (EER, FAR/FRR, ROC AUC) plus unlinkability and irreversibility metrics defined per ISO/IEC 24745
general_score_metric: EER (Equal Error Rate) for recognition; modality-specific unlinkability/irreversibility measures for privacy
typical_sota_score: varies by modality; typically EERs in the low single digits to low double digits (≈1–10%) depending on modality and setup
reputation: Academic benchmark with open-source code that is of interest in biometric privacy/security research but not a widely standardized community benchmark.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; modality-dependent results and dataset sizes; privacy-sensitive data and reproducibility depend on access to original biometric datasets; performance and privacy trade-offs vary by scheme and biometric trait.
